questions.q: Why does this lesson say a full mock review board, combining all five prior skills at once, matters at this point in the course?
options: Because mock review boards are only useful for memorizing Salesforce trivia

Because a real review board exercises requirements extraction, comparing alternatives, naming risks/assumptions, presenting, and handling feedback all at once, under pressure — not any one skill in isolation
Because each skill lesson up to this point was actually redundant with the others
Because a mock review eliminates the need to ever present to a real audience
questions.explain: Lessons 9 through 13 each isolated one skill. A real review board tests all of them together, under time pressure, with unscripted follow-up questions — which is exactly what this lesson's mock session is designed to simulate.

questions.q: Which panel-question category specifically asks the architect to restate the tradeoff behind their recommendation rather than just the recommendation itself?
options: "What's your rollback plan if this is wrong?"
"Who disagrees with you, and why might they be right?"
"Why not the alternative?"
"What breaks this at scale?"
questions.explain: "Why not the alternative" forces the architect to explain why the other option lost, which requires restating the comparison and its tradeoffs rather than simply repeating why the chosen design is good.

questions.q: This lesson says three of its five panel-question categories focus on something specific about a design. What is it?
options: The design's cost estimate alone
Whether the design uses the newest Salesforce feature available
The visual quality of the presentation slides
The boundaries of the design — what it deliberately excludes, how it fails at scale, and how it could be reversed — rather than its center
questions.explain: "What breaks this at scale," "what did you deliberately not solve," and "who disagrees with you" all probe the edges of the design rather than the core recommendation — testing whether the architect has genuinely thought through the design's limits, not just its strengths.

questions.q: What does this lesson identify as the most common way an otherwise well-prepared candidate underperforms in a real review?
options: Treating boundary questions (scale, scope, rollback, disagreement) as attacks to deflect rather than as the actual substance being tested
Spending too much time explaining the chosen design's center in detail
Using too many diagrams in the presentation
Presenting the alternatives considered before the recommended design
questions.explain: A well-prepared architect can usually explain their own recommendation clearly. Underperformance typically comes from treating the harder boundary questions as something to deflect, rather than recognizing that those questions are the actual substance a review board is testing.

questions.q: What does this lesson say about Salesforce's own CTA certification review-board round, based on real candidate and Salesforce-published accounts?
options: It has no live questioning component at all — only a written submission
It includes a live presentation followed by panel Q&A where judges probe gaps, suboptimal choices, and unexplained rationale in the candidate's design
It only tests multiple-choice Salesforce trivia with no design component
It is identical in format to this lesson's mock session, with no additional time pressure
questions.explain: Real accounts of the CTA review board describe a timed presentation followed by a Q&A round where judges specifically probe missed requirements, suboptimal design choices, and any rationale the candidate didn't explain — the same boundary-testing substance this lesson's mock session practices, at much higher stakes.
